transcript: All Nighter by Natalie Margolin is the kind of play that charmingly drops you into a world that's much smaller than the one we're actually in. Five close friends and roommates meet up to study and complete their last college assignments, and as the hours pass and stress heightens, secrets spill and tensions boil over. I think this play does a good job of not trying to do too much — the scope is contained, every character is well-formed, and the progression feels natural. This is a comedy, though I credit Julia Lester for the vast majority of the comedy here. She plays the quirkiest character and arguably steals the show with how unhinged she is. I thought everyone gave solid performances and the pacing was really strong, especially for the third preview. I don't think I'm gonna remember too much about this play in a year, but that's totally fine. This is not some sort of life-changing theater piece, but it's not trying to be. It was just fun and somewhat nostalgic to invest in these college-level problems, many of which inevitably become quite trivial in the grand scheme of things. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: Creator recommends the play as fun and well-crafted with strong performances, while noting it's not memorable or life-changing — a clear positive with caveats.
